newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean banks to discuss rescue plan for Kia.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean banks to discuss rescue plan for Kia.

text.p: South Korean banks will meet on Monday to discuss ways of bailing out the ailing Kia Group, including financial aid and sell-offs of some of the group's units, officials at Korea First Bank said.
"The meeting of creditor banks, we expect, will produce a rough framework of a rescue scheme for the Kia Group," said Rha Byung-rok, a spokesman at Korea First, a main Kia creditor.
"The emergency meeting was planned because something should be done before the July 30 meeting aimed at mapping out a detailed rescue plan," he said.
On Tuesday, local banks decided to rescue the troubled Kia Group, South Korea's eighth largest conglomerate.
The group ran into financial difficulty following a slump in domestic sales of its carmaking flagship Kia Motors at home and heavy capital investment by its steelmaking unit Kia Steel.
A domestic newspaper said Korea First was planning to merge Kia Motors with its supporting units and sell off other Kia affiliates, including Asia Motors and Kia Steel.
The bank was quoted as saying the current Kia management would be in place to promote its self-rescue programme.
